column90: Alpine was more engaged in the process this year, good to see. There is more quality evidence of tracked metrics in physical, technical and gaps through athlete profile. Some better visibility on testing and race times of PD2. Gap analysis was quite clear. Ability to intervene in the competition phase was limited but reasonable in context. Sport costs around weather have been quite impactful to bottom line financial strain. Limited access to Europe this year. Great video analysis, heart rate and bronco informed modifications to fitness. Good monitoring of imbalances between book end FMS engagements. NCCP gaps are monitored well, HP is the biggest gap but challenging to address at the club level. Minimum standards are in place and clear strategies to offer programming to address. EE use of funds is clear and consistently applied. reporting standards were much better this year. The change in funds had the desired affect in my view.
column91: Good presentation, lots of data and info presented on athletes, good level of monitoring of speed, strength and power along with the mental prep side. Coach education at a high level with a big emphasis on PD.
column92: Strong presentation and good to have Morgan (Head Coach) report on the athlete profiles.  Good to see data informing decision making and some level of engagement with athletes through performance plans (seemed like every 3-4 months). Some comments on monitoring regional FIS level athletes and ACA beginning to track fitness testing standards across Canada.  Limited data management strategy, but certainly have potential given the data that is being captured.  Alpine does coaching well and benefits from coach longevity in the system, that said, younger (particularly female) coaches are harder to recruit into full-time coaching roles, and the gap to HP often takes a lot of experience.  Pathway to National programs seems dubious and while ACA has Devo team, athletes will likely decide whether the cost benefit is greater to go to the NCAA or stay with ACA (Pay to play).  From an athlete perspective, being able to go to university and continue to race is an advantage over committing the same time and resources to the Devo team.   EE funds are used toward program enhancement with good understanding where funds may be deployed.

column90: Good presentation and inclusion from other people to provide information.   Good to see Jenn Trew (Gym Can) in attendance.   Good to see the application of the skills matrix in MAG program and long term perspective on skill development versus code of points.  Good evidence from TG on strength interventions but no data to support what is happening.  That said,  CSI Pacific involved and can help in tracking data.  WAG remains a bit of an outlier in the system of gymnastics, where GymBC seems to have more impact in MAG and TG.  Athlete performance advisors are likely a good initiative if modelled off of other sports and personal coaches and athletes are monitored on consistent KPIs to inform athlete performance conversations.
column91: Great presentation by GymBC, There is a range of metrics being tracked from MAG and TG. For MAG, there was a clear outline of skills and how they were scored over the year. For TG they did an excellent job outlining jump height as a KPI and how they plan to improve and monitor. An area for improvement could be around MAGs targeted approach to improve KPIs, as well as a plan to improve collaboration from WAG, as this was stated as a gap.
column92: Mag passport outlines the needs around score advancement and there is some evidence of timing for skills to be implemented. Repetition of skills is still outlined and competition scores are still the main KPI and intervention. Really good to hear that there is more wholistic monitoring of athlete health and focus.  Trampoline has much clearer strategy on how to get to a system level way to measure success. Although it is all still in the developing stage so there is limited evidence to present. NCCP was presented in a socialized mentorship approach mostly through Mens camps and tramp again. This hints to more of a clear project strategy that needs more direction. Not clear how NCCP standards are being upheld in the club, only the FOP. Good to see a science based project emerging with Sport Sask. Program is trending up, but still has a ways to go. EE funds are spent, but the detail is not clear as it could be.
column93: Moving in the right direction, little influence at the club level but they are trying to build relationships.

column90: A presentation that seems to defend the use of EE funding and barriers/challenges to aligning to EE standards.  While I agree that having many different events can be challenging, the process to use data informed decision making can be consistently applied across the events.  What will be different is the type of data chosen.  Coaching remains a common issue where There does not seem to be the same interaction with coaches that similar sports enjoy (swimming, xcountry).  Use of EE funding is allocated to team based projects largely around attendance at national championships.  While this is unique for athletics, it does raise some questions whether there are some camp based elements that could be included as staging to these events.
column91: Little contact with athletes outside of Team BC events. Working on PD events and hired a coach developer, more qualified coaches with Team BC and offer coach development grants. Suggest gaps in what NCCP offers and what coaches need, BCA instituting minimum standards in coaching in BC.
column92: Use of funds is clearly articulated but is most directed to technical leadership and performance participation BC Team programming. Good addition of IST travel, but is 6 weeks out enough time to create positive intervention...and are any interventions provided tracked to understand performance potential? The plan outlined was largely driven by results. Despite higher standards it hasn't yielded more visibility with coaches. I did not see a clear plan, as outlined in their letter, to better articulate deliverables. The future state of programming proposed is more aligned to the desired visibility level and engagement with club based programming. There could be better use of IST interventions with targeted populations.  Hopefully this is the future state. Meghann does see open to learning and advancing or getting input into the strategy, but it would be great to see more rapid change and a culture shift toward a targeting strategy and greater program insights.

column90: Funding use was skipped. Some good mentorship for coaches but no clear plan to address NCCP gaps. No evidence of testing data changes, good evidence of athlete programming, small group coaching and targeted competition/skill development opportunities. Would love to see the mico KPIs that are monitored to show change against the macro KPI (ie dribble hand off or pick and roll)
column91: Good presentation however lacking in concrete evidence. Didn't identify any KPI's and how to improve these through testing procedures.  Did not indicate if they have any diagnostics that would follow an FMS .Not clear if fitness testing is making any difference. Some good work going on but I feel that they need to become more targeted with the EE funds and use the money they generate for HP to 'touch everyone in the program'.
column92: Similar presentation to previous years - Anecdotal KPIs with limited data to inform progression over time.  Need to follow up on targeted list and ensure they are registering both athlete and coaches.  Coach pathway is still challenging and limited by NCCP qualifications.  Pathway progression will always struggle until they are able to enhance programming in nextgen space which is largely the role of post-secondary institutions and need NSO leadership to change the paradigm.  SSSM is solid and they are able to 'safeguard' athletes that are in the provincial program.  Also good to know that they are identifying athletes that can move to a higher level as opposed to athletes that 'survive' club and HS programming.

column90: Great presentation. Stronger this year than last and kept to timing while hitting the majority of areas we are looking to see with a good level of detail. Would like to see the change to stronger data systems, but they do an excellent job with what they have. Good report card, system supports and excellent coach standards with club relationships
column91: Really solid presentation and evidence.  Nice to know that there is a bit of a database behind the athlete report cards.  Good overview of PD athletes who are actively registered and one attending CSS in PG.  Nice overview of IPP and Annual plans and how gaps inform the training process. Good overall program interventions and use of EE funding.  It would be good to identify other strategies (DND) to keep athletes in pathway longer which is happening to some degree.  Also curious how the data can be secured so that more analysis can be done on year on year improvement.  Important to ensure ongoing succession with Jessica going on maternity leave.
column92: Some very strong evidence provided. Starting to see good results within Canada and is putting BC athletes on the Olympic team. Great storytelling and EE funds are being put to good use. More athletes are being retained in the system and training for longer.

column90: A good program is clearly improving. Stronger technique analytics are being paired with very good fitness and strength tracking. I like that they are showing clear KPI's and interventions across both key disciplines. Not many sports are doing this well. Strong club integration, despite a small active athlete pool this is still very good. NSO benchmarks are well informed into the programming. They have NCCP trainers and evaluators who can support this system, but as with many sports can overly training when they want, rather need the NSO to take the lead. Good service engagements for testing, I like their service approach of sponsor or low cost with high value to the program dollars. Strong mentor programs and strategies to build next gen coaches. Well engaged in viaSport mentorship programs. IST is engaged and they are widening the reach and frequency. They expressed some challenges with rowing and u-sport. They have some strategies but could do more to keep folks engaged when they move into other age categories that are more aligned to a u-sport path.
column91: Great presentation by Canoe/Kayak. There is a ton of metric tracking from comp standards, technical, physical, training volume, mental performance, and health. The coach development was well done, with monthly PD sessions and mentorship opportunities. Overall great information, an area for improvement would be to be concise on what what they are tracking, how they are addressing it, and a follow up with improvements.
column92: Presented some thorough data around the athlete testing and tracking. Some really good work on the coaching side particularly around coach mentorship.

column90: Cross Country is clearly leading in this space. They have strong fund diversification that allows them to build strong strategy and commit to a high level of club engagement, streamlined data solutions and evidence based interventions. Athlete agreements and minimum coach standards are in place. They have good line of site on gaps in coaching and have a willingness to engage with viaSport on furthering the impact. Clear use of funds with good understanding of the impact in each pillar.
column91: Very solid presentation with highly sophisticated use of data to inform decision making.  Clearly meeting all of the EE objectives and able to speak to program enhancements.  The presentation would be good to share with other PSOs in future powering podiums.  Need to examine how data integrations can be share across sector to preserve CSI Pacific IP, but help to build data infrastructure for other sports.   Also good to follow up on Comp-Dev multi sport delivery and how to tailor deliver to CC Coaches.  It would be good for CCBC to identify a coach for UBC program.

column90: Curl BC had a great presentation! They have a high standard for testing and monitoring, and a lot of work has gone in to the development of this. It is great that they are combining technical/tactical video analysis with physical testing and ensuring it is accessible for athletes across the province. From a coaching perspective, they provide various opportunities for coaches - comp coach courses, encouraging other females to do the CAC WAGE program, Curl BC rockslide camp - on/off ice support and HP coach development program which includes 6-7 virtual workshops for coaching like philosophy/goal setting. They did a good job highlighting their funding and future goals as well.
column91: Excellent presentation by Kayla and Lindsay with support from Melissa and Scott.  Clear evidence of data tracking of KPIs and fitness results for targeted athletes with some ability to create athlete report cards (IPP).  Nice to see ongoing implementation of athlete journal.  In addition, some good information in interventions including S&C and technical feedback using video and curling specific technology.  While they are centralizing data, they could use support in report generation which could be enhanced through CSI Pacific data solutions.  Good to hear some strategies on how to use data to impact athlete personal or team coaches in a decentralized program, but more collaboration is desired in personal coach engagement.   Some good strategies around coaching education with some evidence for Comp-intro coaches.  While provincial coaches have or achieving Comp-Dev certification, it was not clear if there was a pathway to support HP coaches obtaining NCCP Comp-Dev qualification particularly for those coaches supporting more professional teams.  Excellent breakdown of EE expenditures and use of money, with some funding leveraged through CAC WAGE program which is ending for the next fiscal.   Nice to see that Kayla has applied for the UBC program.
column92: Programming continues on a positive trend. There are clear enhancements in equipment, quality of analytics deep into the PD2 level. The organization is leading practices in Curling Canada programming. They have good plans to address NCCP deficits and have a good mentorship strategy around coaching, that said their are significant NCCP and cultural gaps to over come. Dedicated HP training environments are well resourced, Victoria more so and new testing is coming on board. Added S&C components and better monitoring are showing results. Interventions on physical and technical are clear. Tactical intervention is missing a bit, would love to see what kind of tracking could be designed around skip analysis. Great work on articulating budget and money use EE and full performance portfolio.
column93: Thorough presentation of KPI's and fitness testing. Shared financials and presented what they want to tackle next year. Understand the coaching gaps and have a plan to try and support coaches with PD. Regional centers working well and Victoria center now a regional performance center.

column90: Cycling BC had a great presentation. They clearly identified gaps with both athletes (anaerobic power and sustained aerobic capacity). They explained how they will address these gaps while using their YTP. Opportunities for mentorship through camps/high performance projects were highlighted for coaches, as well as utilizing CSI initiatives - ex. UBC program. Funding was mentioned for international race exposure, support athlete monitoring and testing and coach opportunities. An area of improvement could be to provide specific examples of initiatives to help improve the program and coaching opportunities (what's the idea, when is it being implemented, how can individuals access it etc.). Also providing more in-depth monitoring for coaches/athletes - ex using training peaks to add in pieces for strength and conditioning in addition to training loads from training peaks or power monitoring.
column91: Good data from training peaks on ride training based programs, there is some disconnect between what i happening in the gym or fms to inform what's happing on bike. The two are tracked but would love to see this more linked and provided in a visualization (like an athlete report card) describing the gaps and successes with the why behind that. Athletes receive great projects that will help them as they reach to the next level. Good club and personal coach connection. Would just like to see that both ends of the path for the athlete (personal coach to NSO) are more informed about how athletes are tracking toward NSO benchmarks. The perfect outcome would be that the NSO is better informed on athletes consistently achieving benchmarks and kpi's to inform selection rather than the current single race out come equals selection approach. Coach data and certification standards need to be addressed better by the NSO. It might help if the NSO is more aware that this is a reporting requirement in BC to help them clean the locker data.
column92: Shared KPI's and how data is driving coaching interventions. Not much info on athlete testing, athletes are using training peaks and strava for monitoring and data is shared around the group but doesn't seem to be have any security around it. Much more focused presentation than the previous years.
column93: Tara was well prepared for the meeting and did a good job of updating on specific evidence related to the provincial program.  It is good to see more ability to track data, but lack of a centralized data management system makes it difficult to pull data into multi KPI reports.  That said, their is evidence that targeted athlete conversations are happening with personal coaches and these conversations are informed by data through training peaks or power profiling.  There is a sense that the relationships with coaches are more conducive to provincial programming and good to see comp and camp based projects to incentivize targeted athletes, providing high quality athlete experiences.   Coach pathway is a bit of a concern, and while there are good initiatives to engage coaches in the province with professional development, there seems to be a gap in NCCP pathway with many coach lacking or unable to get Comp-Dev status.  Good evidence provided for use of EE funding but may want to show breakdown of project costs and how EE funds are used specifically within a given project (i.e. athlete fees, coaching, travel/accommodation, etc..)

column90: Good presentation on two provincial level divers from Tommy.  Igor was not available for the call due to family circumstances.  Clear KPIs based on code of points, but good observations in adapting (maximizing) training plan due to Saanich pool closure in the fall.  The opportunity to do dryland did have an impact on diving skills (Flexibility).  The pool closure while contributing to a decrease in overall training but had some positive impact on overall training which seem to impact in pool skills.  Good linkages with NSO as Tommy is playing a HP lead role for younger age groups.  Diving Canada is prioritizing syncho diving which has some exposure at the provincial level, but limited by suitable partners which may be in a different club or province.   PSO is doing a great job helping coaches achieve NCCP comp-dev status and proactive approach to identifying junior coaches in BC based High Performance Grants.  Also good to see that 5 coaches attended Diving Canada Camp.  Use of EE funds are well are used to support technical leadership, however, there are concerns if the funds are being used to provide direct athlete funding as opposed to PSO project based funding.  Need to liaise with Igor to discuss LOU and Sprot Science support which would be align to project based enhancement.
column91: Great presentation from Diving BC. They did well at outlining what they wanted to impact (ex. Jackson - pike connection or adding new dives - 4 new total) and listed how they impacted KPIs by describing interventions like stretching and how they utilized progressive overload. It was great to see a YTP for Nixon, seems to follow appropriate progressions through the year.  While some BC based athletes might get assessments done from a technical piece but no physical testing for assessment. BC diving was able to outline how they support coaches - Workshops for coaches + PSO helps contribute to this. HPAD camps are subsidized by PSO as well and coaches from all over the province allowed to attend. An area of improvement from a coaching side would be to highlight specific gaps for coaching, interventions implemented, and follow up on with coaches on how it went the following year. For ex. If it was psychology - what was presented or what takeaways did the coaches have and how did it go implementing it? Overall well done.
column92: Not sure how money is being allocated and who by. Is it benefiting a few athletes or is it across the PSO HP system to support enhancements. Facing some facility challenges over the next 12-18 months. I found evidence was anecdotal and no concrete examples of data informed decision making.
column93: The dive program is not always clear on how funds impact targeted athletes who are not in the NSO targeted pool. Dollars seem very focused on a select few athletes rather than depth of tracking, monitoring and interventions down the list. Good evidence of specific athlete changes over time. Improved S&C programming for the small pool of top athletes is clearly making an impact. Unsure how club funds or athlete based funding aligns to system enhancement. It would be great to see more directed program benefit like S&C at the club level for targeted athletes (more directed). Coaching success with Canada Games is great, but Dive Can needs to find better ways of meeting the needs of pathway coaches. This limits planning for the PSO and may limit club understanding of HP needs, due to lack of complete education. Dive needs some support further down the pathway (note for viaSport to support)

column90: Good evidence of player assessment happening at PSO level and some communication with NSO and club level coaches.  That said, it is unclear how NSO defines Nextgen and are targeting athletes in the PSO space as opposed to extending the pathway beyond PSO programming.  This creates some confusion over athlete programming, but it does happen more organically as NSO/PSO coaches are managing programming likely in an informal manner.  Mark indicated that the NSO is identifying these athlete so that they can take a variety of national team programs away to competition.  This may actually help FHBC to identify streams toward Higher quality competition, but there needs to be some structure around identification and commitment of athlete to PSO programming (likely prior to) NSO enhance projects.   If managed correctly it could help to identify coaches for NSO projects.  The risk is that the NSO is using these projects as a quasi academy based programming that may not be well managed from an athlete standpoint.  Coaching qualification is frustrating as comp-dev programming is not readily available and or NCCP locker has not been updated.
column91: Good evidence provided on all areas. More testing of athletes and MPC support available to PD athletes. Concerns over the large number of athletes that are being pulled up to CAN DEV level by NSO. Its clear that FHBC are working hard to enhance their programming.
column92: Some positive shifts into a more performance thinking. The increased use of S&C is helpful in monitoring but curious to see what KPI's look like on Tech & Tac when they have a style of play metric. Not clear on how talent id evaluation remains consistent or what that rubric looks like (ie Gym Passport?) Good to see Comp Dev is finally approved, they need some system tools like evaluation capacity and better locker data to progress. Better alignment with the NSO and system supports is progress.

column90: Danielle has transitioned into CEO role and needs to hire a technical lead which may occur by April 2026.  Overall there was some good evidence of consistent fitness testing, however, it was difficult to determine the type of off-ice interventions being made and how the S&C program dovetails into the athlete/coach YTP.  That said, if Skate BC is providing the S&C program and other sport science enhancement, they are doing a good job in tailoring an overall PSO YTP that can fit individualized (personal coach) training plans.  I am still not certain how much formalized Performance Planning is driven by the individual coach and would recommend that Skate BC has coaches come into the EE meeting to discuss their programming.  While good alignment to NSO Nextgen fitness measures, there could be enhancements to testing and ensuring that the test data can inform programming as opposed to athlete maturation which can be tricky for younger athletes.   There was some acknowledgement of pathway changes in Skate Canada, and therefore good to update targeting criteria.  It would be good to look at historical conversion data to help inform how athletes are moving through the pathway.  Hoping that coaches are able enhance coaching professional development and it would be good to see if UBC HPCTL may be an option for some coaches.
column91: Figure Skating BC did a great job. They provided testing metrics for 2 of their athletes, and outlined some interventions such as strength and conditioning to enhance strength and power to help with technical skills. An area of improvement could be around, including more strategic plans for interventions following testing, as well as planning to improve female qualification. Lastly, a more clear outline regarding priority for funds and specific projects based on gaps identified.
column92: Improved clarity around program insights. Good to see that testing has been implemented and results are tracked. Still challenged to engage MPC despite the need being identified, but clearly better use of Sport Science Sport Med overall. It would be good to have better insights into fitness standards, what interventions or programming are prescribed and progress is monitored beyond testing periods. NCCP model is strong but there are identified gaps in aging coaches. Mentorship is being implemented to try to capture next gen coaches. Gap analysis was better than previous years. Some deeper understanding of how programming and SS/SM inform athlete advancement. Greater consistency of protocol and coach to coach testing variance would be good to see. Camp environment and increased code of points/skill acquisition monitoring are clear enhancements from previous reporting. Breakdown of funding is know but not specifically shared.
column93: More intentional around fitness testing than in previous year. PSO develops YTP but doesn't have any way to enforce its use with coaches. Data stored centrally and coaches have access. Some challenges in decentralization but Skate recognizes these challenges. Some opportunities to collaborate with the PSO to help build and support programming.

column90: Good presentation, showed information on fitness testing and an improvement in performance. Informed in interventions with athletes and also shared programming details. Provided good information on where EE $'s are going and they are working hard in the coaching space.
column91: I liked Graham's tactic on presenting one athlete with the lens of good intervention and gap analysis to change performance and testing outcomes, while the other athlete was more focused on YTP use and programming to enhance their performance. Both had clear gap analysis. All lead to successful outcomes.  They are improving their approach to NCCP and certifying evaluators to support system enhancement was great to see. Good EDI coach initiative too. Strong use of CSI services and clearly better club engagement to talent id.
column92: Very good presentation particularly identifying athlete monitoring and coaching initiatives.  Clear advantage in liaising with CSI Pacific to help with diagnostics and enhanced programming.  While not presented, Josh did outline the use of EE funding.   That said, they are looking to track EE funding.   Good evidence overall and good linkages emerging between clubs, PSO and NSO programming for both athletes and coaches.

column90: Judo BC has incorporated some great initiatives with mental performance tactics and performance testing. However, an area of improvement could be around including timelines and actionable steps in their YTP for athletes to achieve their goals whether that's technical, tactical, or physiological. In addition, funding info was provided per athlete, but a summary slide of all expenses and how it was utilized or areas they would like to focus on for the following year would be great.
column91: Solid presentation and good examples of athlete and coach engagement in provincial program.  Certainly seems to be good support of the provincial program from local coaches and athletes.  Coach 2.0 working well to develop coaches and increase NCCP comp dev qualifications.  Clear standards and incentives are in place to leverage athlete and coach commitment.   Priority of EE funding targeted at Coaching, Travel, and IST support.  Good example of how Provincial program can drive club level coaching and athlete development.
column92: Some good information but not much information about how to win and performing on demand. No plan ion place for athletes from outside the LM other than moving to the LM?
column93: Very high quality program with smart physical benchmarking and testing strategies in place. Addition of an AC has increased capacity to develop athletes. Digging a bit deeper on tactical win % might help advance the already strong metrics and standards. Good competition enhancements and testing with CSI. Clear next steps around MPC use and there is a strong coaching progression in place. Good tools for athlete buy in and a new model for athlete self assessment and learning outcome mapping.

column90: Good presentation and provided some good evidence around what is happening in Rowing. They are on top of things and building relationships with local clubs and schools. Identified KPI's and showed testing data over a period of time that showed improvements. Data is informing technical decisions. Gaps in coaching have been identified and mentorship is being deployed to support coaches. EE funds used to fill the gap of Canada Games and Rowing will be back in the CG in 2029.
column91: Rowing BC outlined the performance metrics they are tracking well, as well as how they are supporting coaches. It's great that there is more of an initiative to travel to individual clubs to work 1:1 with the coaches and I like that a coach education session was provided! An area to address could be how the performance testing is going to impact an athletes YTP as well as specific breakdown in funding allocation to these initiatives.
column92: Strong presentation and quality evidence of provincial programming.  Good to see the evolution of BC Rowing with Terry in Technical leadership position.  Clear that he is able to build trust with local coaches.  Recommend continuing relationship with CSI Pacific on LOU and leveraging other performance services.  CSI Pacific could assist in creating report cards based on current data which would help drive discussion with coaches and value add for those athletes attending Rowing BC project.  Also recommend to update targeted coach list to include coaches having an impact on provincial programming and ensure NCCP locker is up to date.
column93: Terry had a stronger presentation this year that last in areas of fitness testing and use of EE funds for project based and csi opportunities. There is a lot of general erg testing but no clear, by athlete, intervention mapping that demonstrates why they are seeing change in erg testing to the positive. Highly dependent on the prep school model to talent. Despite the strong link for talent, there is a lack of visibility in to the DTE or ability to connect athlete training to provincial programing. So good one on one coaching work and nice to see some progress on the advancing coaches in the prep environment to the Comp Dev standard. Demonstrated ability to link athlete to strong schools in the US and still see them return. It would be great to see if they can get more contact in the college DTE.

column90: About 80% of the presentation was geared toward performance participation and largely focused on Age grade competitions.  That said, BC Rugby influencing competition structure at senior level to help support national team identification.  Women's pathway is well identified with legitimate USPORT opportunities for best players and BC Rugby supporting some programming at this level.  Men's pathway is hard to articulate beyond U18/19.  No indication on how EE funds are being used to enhance programming.  Possibly 3 enhancements could be identified, 1. International Sevens tournament in December, 2. Testing implementation, but need for better off-field programming and data tracking, 3. Need to target and identify coaches for Comp-Dev training (i.e. if RC cannot deliver this, then pay for coaches to go to NZ to do it).  It would be good to articulate a team sport strategy that directs EE funding as this may help PSO to influence Local level and inform better programming.  (i.e. High Quality Competition, Sport Science embedded programming, targeted coach development).
column91: Good presentation, lots of information on athletes and presented the schedules and possible progression opportunities over the next 2 years. Presented thorough information on coaching development program and how they are addressing the challenges of certification through World Rugby.
column92: limited visibility on use of funds, Dave identified areas of EE fund priority more than John did. Coaching gaps at the tactical level meet desired level, but technical and testing skills are lacking. No current solve for this, but there is a change to introduce a Comp Int Advance that may be an opportunity to strengthen given the restriction on Comp Dev access. PSO athlete monitoring has improved and more evidence of technical and fitness tools used to measure. Limited buy in or alignment with Club or NSO. Targeted international tour. Starting to see IST in the U17. Not clear around targeted outcomes and pathway has limited ability to target talent or 7s v 15s target. There is not a lot of opportunity for PSO visibility given the seasonal plan. There are clear opportunities to better regulate athlete load but not a clear strategy to engage in change management or get school and club sport to buy in.

column90: Great improvements in delivery over the past few years. Clearly recognizes value of CSI services in providing deeper insights and stronger athlete improvements. Much more data informed. I also appreciate the targeted boat choice. Others can learn from this tactic. I would love to see more detail on athletes outside the vic/van area to get a better picture of reach. Good to see NSO alignment improve. Needs a greater strategy on how to monitor and develop engagement strategies for coach development. Possible better insight and programming for PD2 athletes. Could use a clear picture of how funds are spent but it seems clear that IST is a priority for funds.
column91: Strong evidence of physical preparation data informed decision making,  things are working well in this space for Sailing. Starting now to look at coach development a little further down the pathway, good numbers on clinics and they seem to be on top of this and know what coaches are certified. Sailing moving in the right direction-Good presentation.
column92: Well prepared with some good evidence of evolving the sailing HP program.  Certainly there is benefit to engaging CSI Pacific practitioners in the S&C space which can be added to with other disciplines in future LOUs.  Also opportunity to look at Data Solutions and creating IPP / Athlete report card.  Good to see athletes moving through the pathway and PSO taking on the NSO DTE responsibilities.   Need collaboration with NSO to identify athlete ready high quality competition opportunities and informing the level of competition off of data.  (i.e. very good example linking strength data to sailing at high wind speeds).

column90: Evidence of thorough tracking and data informed decisions, they have a good understanding of where the gaps are in coaching and presented a good action plan to provide PD to coaches.
column91: Solid presentation and good evidence of athlete programming.  Nice to see growth at club level and maturity of clubs to produce snowboard programs. Good identification of Slopestyle athletes which seems to be priority at local level as many athletes do not have consistent access to SBX tracks.  Most evidence is obviously in SBX as BC team has parallel program to NSO.  Good to see slopestyle athletes being put into provincial programming and supported with provincial resources.  Would encourage ongoing growth in clubs.
column92: Still a very strong program. Good to see a number or age ranges for programming and a strategy around offering boardx as an option in a camp setting for slope athletes. Strong program standards in place, event and self monitored data to highlight performance insights and energy transfer efficiencies. Clear gap analysis and programming/race strategy. Testing is consistent and sport specific. Good growth in club development in the Slope space. Would love to see some strategies to build hp path for these athletes. Incoming coach may support this to a greater degree.

column90: Good evidence of well monitored athletes with improvements to monitoring and testing in Camp settings. Well managed engagement with clubs to get a variety of testing data. Some are more science based and others more test set exclusive. Gaps for each swimmer were clear as was coach interventions but there is limited ability for the PSO to lean in to ensure outcomes are being seen. Great coach engagement and clearly gap to intervention strategy. Para development steps are excellent. Clear budget strategy and enhancements. Race Tech evidence is great, would love to see the uptake rate over time. Opportunity to engage CSI in camp to get some level set across the athlete population.
column91: Good presentation and shared some relevant information. Registration numbers across the province are outpacing population share. Identified that clubs are not accountable to Swim BC so they are trying to build relationships with clubs by providing resources. Good work being done in the coach ed space in particular in the area of PD through the Swim BC Congress.
column92: Swimming BC provided a great outline of their in-water performance tracking metrics, as well as the breakdown in funding allocation. Some areas of improvement could be around offering performance testing during camp settings which would allow for some standardized results. Also, this could be paired with the application of biomechanics, strength and conditioning, to see how it impacts metrics collected from their software.
column93: Very strong presentation that covered all of the areas required.  Excellent process of going out to selected coaches to get an update on targeted athletes.  Interesting whether that type of debrief is could be formalized.  Good tool (data) to inform athlete performance data and tracking, however, KPI testing at the club level is quite varied (Can it be standardized and for what purpose?).  Curious whether project based funding approach would have a bigger impact particularly with this type of sport which lacks a provincial program, but supports club based development pathways.  Some good opportunity to engage CSI Pacific for Sport science whether on individual athlete level (Nutrition or MPC) versus group based access (Physiology or S&C).

column90: As usual Kelly has strong programming and data informed competition and athlete development strategies. Love the cost barrier reduction for provincial team athletes. Very strong use of funding in smart ways to target effective competitive enhancements. As a camp based sport, i would love to see where testing and services support athletes outside the vic dte. When comparing similar size, scope and quality of programming, there seems to be greater regional reach in other programs, especially around PD2 athlete. Overall, very effective programming and tie ins with key partners like 94 forward and uvic
column91: Lots of good things going on that are providing more options for more athletes and building the program out by learning from other programs. Not much info on NCCP standards but there is a significant amount of PD going on for coaches. Using 94Forward to support triathlon development by paying coaches salaries. Can EE $'s be spent specifically on testing, diagnostics, nutrition and MPC support.
column92: Very good evidence of planning and monitoring of athlete KPIs and acknowledging a need for a more integrated data reporting and visualization.  Great evidence on Provincial Developmental athletes.  Really good to see the relationship with Uvic to extend meaningful sport engagement after High School.  Victoria Triathlon Center is a good opportunity to leverage partnership and provide high quality athlete extensions to the Olympic pathway.  I really like the high quality competition projects as this is a key driver to help inform athlete readiness in a provincial (Friendly) environment as opposed to NSO environments that may be more performance on demand at both Junior and Senior level.

column90: Adrian was well prepared for the meeting highlighting general athlete KPIs and Fitness testing.  Overall some good evidence of performance participation, with team BC programming providing the basis for targeted athlete support.  Some evidence of deploying S&C programming to team BC athletes but little in the way of monitoring athlete compliance or integrated programming into the club system.  Also some enhancement in mental performance.  Coaching lacks progression toward Comp-Dev standard and it seems difficult to obtain training from Volleyball Canada.  Athlete pathway is not entirely clear with several changes to age grade standards (i.e. CSG age) as well as Volleyball Canada programming which provides enhance programming in the 18U pathway.  USPORT continues to be an opportunity to extend pathway, but limited evidence of how athlete are supported after youth programming.  It would seem that there is a critical number of 18-21 year old athletes who may benefit from  enhanced programming and are not longer under club jurisdiction and likely maturing in College or University programming. A more targeted approach to athlete programming may help to develop athletes who are not receiving high quality programming above 18U, while incentivizing Post Secondary coaches in athlete identification and program enhancement.
column91: Provided evidence of testing which is carried out through a contractor. Trying to work with clubs to build relationships, however don't have eyes on the athletes outside of Team BC camps. Recent changes in staffing are being worked through. Its clear that the sport structure makes it difficult for BC Volleyball to have their own stand alone programming throughout the year and they are looking at different opportunities to grow their presence.
column92: This meeting was better than past meetings. It was still not clear that they have good line of site to the athlete and there are long periods with no monitoring or clarity on the consistency of self monitoring/reporting. Increased evidence of short term use of MPC. Testing in camp settings could be improved but is standardized. I do like the skill analysis tool but it needs to permeated deeper in the club system to allow for better monitoring and working with club coaches to support gap analysis and athlete development. It would be interesting to understand athlete conversion to beach form a talent retention and re engaging them in the HP pathway post 6's career. Good injury and self perception monitoring. Video review sessions add value. Could there be additional enhancement beyond the Nationals, potentially for the targeted group of U18 if the CG focuses more on the U17

column90: Overall a good approach to the meeting by bring in the specific coaches to profile athletes.  Good to see solid application of IPP, and planning process being implemented and formalized.  Data management remains an issue as it is difficult to store, access and analyze data on a scalable fashion over time.  Some opportunity exists for greater IST support which would warrant further conversations around LOU development and potential for para hub model..  High need for centralized summer camp which could be accessed through 94 forward and supported by CSI pacific.  HP cost per athlete are low compared to EE average which may require better reporting.   CSI Pacific could enhance reporting by working directly with sports on reporting process.
column91: Overall fine. Didn't see a progress report on last years pitch to have a centralized HP DTE on the with Simon and Camosun. While they have some aligned KPIs to the NSO with clear benchmarks, the IPPs don't indicate benchmarks or KPI's in the areas being measured. Would like to seen shooting and decision making KPIs (pick & roll, shot v no shot, hold for pick and pop) and Team KPIs for video review (turn over rate, shot decisions on set plays, free throw %). Good evidence of chair technical work to improve efficiencies in defense and build positive decision making for defense. Not a clear outline of use of funds. Coach mentorship is clearly part of it but not a strong focus on IST, or strength based KPIs that would translate to measured performance with accelerometers or other testing. Would have liked to see the difference between supports and interventions for PD1 athletes in another class. Class one is at this level is a very simplistic role.
column92: Thorough presentation around athletes, would like to see a little more data around identified KPI's and testing sets. Spending money on the coaching support and programming has been added at the T2T level, no formal mechanism for data collection or analysis.

column90: BCWSA provided a great presentation, they work towards improving testing and monitoring with their athletes. An area of improvement could be more information around how results directly impact training plans.
column91:
I do have some conflict of interest hear as i have the former HP Manager, developed several of the coaches and staff and am current Head of Officials for wheelchair rugby. 
I do feel they have good grasp of monitoring and lead their NSOs more than is fair for a PSO in Athletics and Tennis. In rugby there are still gaps in access to tracking data from the NSO but they do a good job of connecting skill development to the GMP and have strong understanding of athlete benchmarking in all three sports. Jon has been a good asset for the overall quality of program and is a resource for the other staff. Athletics data is monitored well and is share between coaches and clubs which is more effective than BC Athletics. Tennis has excellent linkage between PSO & NSO. Rugby leadership is well connected to BC. 
Good NCCP strategies and most targeted coaches are achieving strong standards. 
Excellent evidence of financial monitoring
There are gap analysis I'm aware are going on but not fully communicated in the presentation. Questions unpacked a lot of this and supported my understanding better. Overall quite strong and showing signs of strengthening further.
column92: Some good information presented around athletes but could have been more thorough with regard to KPI's. They are moving forward in coach development and see a possible gap ahead. Best in class for financial information.
column93: Very good presentation with a lot of support from BCWCSA staff.  Definitely the staff are informed on the data and seem to be using it to enhance programming.  It was good to have a couple of the coaches on the call to help build out the context in the DTE and reinforce what is being reported.  Overall some quality evidence that show changes over time.  Good discussion at the end of the presentation which really helped to zero in on some of the challenges and potential solutions.  The context around classification is still a bit of a barrier, but it sounded like there was some collaboration at the NSO to try and "steamline" or make appropriate classifications for sport development.  For example, higher point player in WC rugby.  Very good context across three sports which have different interventions, but likely similar themes to maximize HP programming and coaching.  Good to see development on coaching and identifying younger coaches (apprentices) coming into the system.  Excellent overview of EE funding.

column90: Good meeting and discussion around pathway, talent ID and HP programming.  Good overview of KPIs for PD 1 and PD2 athletes, however informing specific interventions or how data informs programming could improve.  Some good evidence of consistent fitness testing, but again limited information on how this is used to inform programming or interactions with personal coaches (Particularly PD 2).  Most PD 1 athlete are centralized at Burnaby Mountain club or SFU.  Good evidence from reporting on helping coaches to get NCCP Comp-Dev status plus some avenues for PD.  There are some challenges that exist to help develop club coach in the pathway and particularly School coaches where there are no standards.  There may be some opportunity to link sport with regional centers to help build capacity whether through facilities or storage.  Definite desire to want to build regional programming in the Kootenay region (Columbia Basin).  EE funds are identified for projects but lacked dollar value, which was somewhat clarified during the discussion.  Good sense that staff want to improve and are open to ideas and feedback.
column91: Nice presentation from Wrestling BC. They are tracking appropriate metrics for wrestling with a good range strength, power, and endurance. I like the testing outline/report, although an area of improvement could be including a rubric for athletes and having standards which can be used to compare their athletes. They identified coaching facilitation as a gap, and area to improve. There are some initiatives to also help improve female coaching in the province. Funding is being directed towards sport science (S&C - equipment/testing, nutrition, MP)
column92: Take opportunity to travel south for competition, trying to get more of a presence around the province outside of the LM, good performance at Canada games. Presented some good data on testing and KPI's. EE money goes into general budget but then lives as a line item within the total budget. Building LF's for the future and they have a good strategy in this area.
column93: This is a very good program. New leadership is starting to strengthen it further, with more detail in the approach and a better gap analysis of all systems. Strong leadership in place technically, the main program gap is breadth. Would love to see the monitoring and testing strategy more connected to the regions that do have good participation. Coaching gap analysis and planning seems to be well thought through with plans to elevate LF and Intro Comp. Excellent investment in performance gaps, technical tactical enhancement with US events. Internal force plate testing tools, vo2 etc clearly enhance the program. Good data tracking and willingness to strengthen further. Look for ways that viaSport relationship can support coach dev and club connection & shared service partners on shipping. Would like to seem better personal coach briefing on the data that the PSO collects to better enhance the club/talent ID DTE.
